item.title: Trump Says His Son Will Pay Back Russian Businessman for Wedding Party
item.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
item.content:encoded: The president said his eldest son, Donald Trump Jr., had decided to return the money, but defended the gift worth hundreds of thousands of dollars as “totally allowed.”

item.title: Mamdani’s Consumer Cop to Begin Tech Oversight Push Within Weeks
item.author: Laura Nahmias and María Paula Mijares Torres
item.content:encoded: New York City’s consumer protection chief said a new enforcement unit to police predatory corporate practices will begin work within weeks, with the gig economy among its priorities.

item.title: NATO Picks Germany’s Top Defense Official to Be Military Chief
item.author: Andrea Palasciano and Marilen Martin
item.content:encoded: NATO chose German General Carsten Breuer to chair the alliance’s military committee in a nod to Berlin’s booming defense industry and rearmament drive.

item.title: Trump Has Tried to Ban Reporters From Government Spaces Before
item.author: Erik Wemple and Michael M. Grynbaum
item.content:encoded: There are several instances where the president made an effort to stifle the work of journalists.

item.title: How Trump’s Trade War Could Hurt Republican Efforts to Hold the Senate
item.author: Tim Balk, Oralandar Brand-Williams and Jesse Ellison
item.content:encoded: In a handful of border states and industrial states that could decide Senate control, the president’s standoff with Canada has drawn criticism from voters, including some who supported him in 2024.

item.title: Dutch Police Break Up Violent Far-Right Protest in The Hague
item.author: Patrick Van Oosterom
item.content:encoded: Dutch police broke up a far-right protest of several hundred demonstrators in The Hague after it turned violent on Saturday.

item.title: JD Vance’s Yale Years Offer Clues to His Politics
item.content:encoded: Vanity Fair contributing writer Chris Whipple spent six months examining JD Vance’s years at Yale Law School, including the influence of professor Amy Chua and previously unreported contacts in which Whipple says Vance offered Hillary Clinton’s 2016 campaign advice on defeating Donald Trump. Whipple is on Bloomberg This Weekend and discusses how his reporting traces Vance’s evolution from a prominent Trump critic to Trump’s vice president, while examining the relationships and experiences that helped shape his political career. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Tariffs Threaten Great Lakes Shipping Tied to Canada Trade
item.author: Brendan Murray
item.content:encoded: The American Century often draws a crowd when the ship pulls into the Port of Duluth-Superior to load Minnesota iron ore. Kids cheer when the captain blasts the fog horn. A voice on the loudspeaker retells the story of how the 1,000-foot-long bulk carrier has sailed the Great Lakes for nearly a half century.

item.title: EU Presses Partners to Deliver Ukraine Funding Ahead of UN Week
item.author: Jorge Valero and Alessandra Migliaccio
item.content:encoded: The European Union is pressing international partners to provide funding to Ukraine as the country faces increasing financing needs amid a tense battlefield situation before the winter.

item.title: CNN, MS NOW Barred From White House After Ban by Trump
item.author: Kevin Whitelaw and Josh Wingrove
item.content:encoded: MS NOW, CNN and Politico said their journalists were denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday after President Donald Trump said he would bar the outlets.

item.title: Sherrod Brown Tries a New Retort to Criticism on Transgender Issues
item.author: Emily Davies
item.content:encoded: A spot from the Senate candidate in Ohio seeks to dismiss the Republican Party’s focus on transgender rights as a distraction from economic issues.

item.title: China Slams US Law Tightening Sanctions on Russia and Iran
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: China criticized the new US law that strengthens sanctions on Russia and extends trade measures on Iran, which was signed late Friday by President Donald Trump.

item.title: Malaysian Minister to Resign after 1MDB Pardon Sparks Criticism
item.author: Anders Melin and Ram Anand
item.content:encoded: Malaysian Transport Minister Anthony Loke said he plans to resign from cabinet in response to the conditional pardon given to former Prime Minister Najib Razak related to his role in one of the largest corruption scandals in modern history.

item.title: Midterm Voting Starts in Key States With Election 45 Days Out
item.author: Caitlin Reilly
item.content:encoded: It’s 45 days before an Election Day that will determine control of Congress for the remainder of President Donald Trump’s second term and 20 states are already mailing ballots to voters. That includes the hard-fought Senate contests in Texas, Michigan and North Carolina.

item.title: US to Return $2.5 Million From Asset Tied to Ex-Gambian Dictator
item.author: Modou Joof
item.content:encoded: The US will transfer $2.5 million recovered from a Maryland property tied to former Gambian dictator Yahya Jammeh to compensate eligible victims of his more than 22-year rule.

item.title: UK Mansion Tax May Expand to Homes Worth Over £1.5 Million
item.author: Harry Wilson
item.content:encoded: The UK’s Labour government is examining plans to expand a new property tax to include homes worth more than £1.5 million ($2 million), according to The Times newspaper, citing unnamed government sources.

item.title: US, China Trade Teams Set to Huddle in New York on AI, Iran
item.author: Colum Murphy, Alicia Diaz and Yash Roy
item.content:encoded: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng will lead talks on trade and other pressure points Sunday in New York ahead of next week’s summit between the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies.

item.title: US Reaches Greenland Deal to End Row That Threatened NATO
item.author: Sanne Wass
item.content:encoded: The US, Denmark and Greenland struck a security deal that expands Washington’s role on the Arctic island, ending for now a long-running diplomatic spat without ceding land to the US.

item.title: US Lifts Sanctions Aimed at Eritrea’s Ruling Party and Military
item.author: Janice Kew
item.content:encoded: The US is letting lapse its five-year national emergency over the conflict and humanitarian crisis in Ethiopia, lifting sanctions on Eritrea’s military, ruling party and other individuals and entities targeted under the measure.

item.title: Russia Warns New U.S. Sanctions Law Would Harm Trump’s Peace Efforts
item.author: Paul Sonne
item.content:encoded: President Trump signed the legislation, named for Senator Lindsey Graham, at the White House, but he has broad leeway to waive its requirements.

item.title: Tracking Assault Weapons Bans Across the Country as Court Battles Continue
item.author: Aishvarya Kavi
item.content:encoded: Here are the states that have sought to limit access to some of the most lethal firearms, as gun restrictions face new legal challenges.

item.title: After North Carolina’s Gerrymander, Democrat Don Davis Trumpets His Centrism in 1st District
item.author: Olivia Diaz
item.content:encoded: Representative Don Davis is seeking re-election in a district redrawn by state lawmakers to lean more Republican.

item.title: Kennedy Center Supporters Rally Amid Fears of Trump’s Demolition
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: Photos of President Trump reviewing a poster board with the title “Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED” spurred the largest gathering yet in support of the performing arts institution.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Issues Rare Air-Raid Alerts for Riyadh
item.author: Fiona MacDonald and Sara Gharaibeh
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabian authorities issued air-raid alerts for Riyadh early Saturday, the first in the capital since the height of the US-Iran war in March and April.

item.title: German Elections on Baltic Coast and Berlin May Seal Merz’s Fate
item.author: Arne Delfs and Michael Nienaber
item.content:encoded: Campaigning in the Baltic port city of Rostock this week, the eastern German state premier seeking to extend her nine-year tenure took Friedrich Merz to task for failing to address surging fuel prices.

item.title: Andy Burnham to Meet Donald Trump as Aides Blame President for Economic Woes
item.author: Alex Wickham
item.content:encoded: Andy Burnham is about to come face-to-face with the man his own officials blame for the UK government’s economic predicament: Donald Trump.

item.title: Air Force Officer Charged After Protesting Trump Says He Spoke to Defend Constitution
item.author: Anushka Patil
item.content:encoded: Major Jason Watson could face court-martial in what could become a rare test of a service member’s right to publicly dissent.

item.title: Japan, US Agree To Deepen Security Ties as Koizumi Stays in Post
item.author: Takashi Mochizuki
item.content:encoded: Japan’s Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth agreed in a phone call to further strengthen security ties after Koizumi retained his post in a cabinet reshuffle by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

item.title: F.A.A. Safety Request for the Top of Trump’s Arch: Eternal Fire
item.author: Luke Broadwater
item.content:encoded: The aviation agency deemed the mammoth arch safe for air travel if it includes a constant flame and other safety measures to help make it visible to planes.

item.title: U.S. and Denmark Reach Security Deal on Greenland, Trump Says
item.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Jeffrey Gettleman and Anton Troianovski
item.content:encoded: The full contours of the deal were unclear, but Denmark and Greenland both indicated they expected an agreement to be signed soon.

item.title: Trump Says He Has Banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico From White House
item.author: Michael M. Grynbaum and Benjamin Mullin
item.content:encoded: The president cited reporting from the outlets that he deemed “fake news.” It was unclear how such a ban would be enforced or defended in court.

item.title: Appeals Court Restricts Trump Administration Deportation Effort
item.author: Mattathias Schwartz
item.content:encoded: The ruling allows migrants to contest deportations to countries other than their place of origin. The case could head to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Republicans Are Now the ‘Elitist’ Party, Voters Say
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: We spoke to independents who have soured on Trump.

item.title: Russia Aims to Inject Chaos Into Elections, U.S. Intelligence Finds
item.author: Dustin Volz, Julian E. Barnes and Steven Lee Myers
item.content:encoded: The Kremlin is once again seeking to undermine confidence in American democracy with online influence campaigns, U.S. officials said.

item.title: F.A.A. to Roll Out New A.I. Tool for Washington Airports
item.author: Aishvarya Kavi and Karoun Demirjian
item.content:encoded: The tool, called SMART, will crunch scheduling and weather data to predict and avoid delays. It will be deployed in the Washington region’s three major airports next week.

item.title: Cost of Iran War Estimated at $43.6 Billion
item.author: Eric Schmitt
item.content:encoded: For the first time, the Pentagon reported costs incurred by each armed service. The figures are almost certainly on the low side, congressional officials said.

item.title: Judge Who Struck Down Trump’s Compensation Fund Asks: Will Trump Just Pay Allies Another Way?
item.author: Alan Feuer
item.content:encoded: The question was raised at a court hearing by a federal judge who has already barred the fund from moving forward.

item.title: Trump Courts North Korea’s Leader, but Might Need China to Reignite the Flame
item.author: Edward Wong
item.content:encoded: President Trump has gotten no love back yet from Kim Jong-un. He could turn to Xi Jinping, China’s leader, to help set up a summit when Mr. Xi visits Washington next week.

item.title: Germany Agrees on €2.5 Billion Fuel Relief, Price Cap Plan
item.author: Kamil Kowalcze
item.content:encoded: Germany’s federal and state governments agreed on a €2.5 billion ($2.9 billion) relief package including a three-month fuel-tax cut from October and plans for a temporary cap on pump prices to cushion motorists and businesses.

item.title: James Talarico, Seeking Black Votes in Texas Senate Rate, Wins Crucial Endorsement
item.author: Neil Vigdor
item.content:encoded: The Congressional Black Caucus’s political wing backed James Talarico, who defeated a Black opponent in the primary. He faces Ken Paxton, the Republican state attorney general, in November.
